newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar's rebound seen capped at 116.50 yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar's rebound seen capped at 116.50 yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar's recovery is likely to be capped at around 116.50 yen on Friday in Asia due to selling by exporters and hedge sales by investors after it fell to a fresh low of 114.70 yen overnight in Europe, dealers said.

The dollar's fall below a 200-day moving average of 116.70 yen in Tokyo on Thursday could keep it on a downward track, although it may take a breather after wild movements earlier this week, said a trust bank dealer.
"That's far from saying that the dollar's downward moves are ending. But it may take a breather today ahead of the weekend after volatile moves," he added.

The trust bank dealer said Japanese life insurers moved to pick up the dollar when it sank to 114.70 yen in London, which helped the dollar push back above 115 yen. He said given such movements, the dollar is likely to stay above 115 yen in Asia.
In New York trade, remarks by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin supported the dollar.

"We have said repeatedly that in our judgment a strong dollar is in the best interest of the United Sates. It results in lower inflation, results in lower interest rates and it thereby helps feed a higher growth rate," said Rubin in a speech to the Investment Company Institute.
A city bank dealer said recent rapid falls of the dollar against the yen resulted in a bounce-back overseas on Thursday, although the dollar could stay on a downward trend.
The dollar had fallen nearly 10 percent from a peak of 127.47 yen on May 1.
Dealers said options-linked stop-loss dollar sales are lined up on the downside, with speculators willing to test them.
The dollar/mark is likely to be directionless, while the mark could stay weak against the yen because of the dollar's recent tumble against the yen, they said.
